# John Ashdown

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c14 P12](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0012), [v5 c21 P1](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0001), [v5 c26 P22](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0022)</sub>
- **Role:** Minister  <sub>[v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c21 P3](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0003), [v5 c26 P22](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0022)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mr. Ashdown  <sub>[v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002)</sub>; Rev. John Ashdown  <sub>[v5 c9 P86](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0086)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Jack  <sub>[v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

John Ashdown has dark hair that hangs in unkempt locks across a high forehead, as well as handsome dark eyes. He possesses thin white hands that have a surprisingly strong, steel grip. Despite sometimes appearing unkempt in a dressing gown and slippers, he retains the posture and demeanor of a gentleman.

_Sources: [v5 c13 P4](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0004), [v5 c14 P12](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0012), [v5 c14 P18](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0018)_

## Personality

Underneath a shy, distant, and pale exterior, John Ashdown harbors a boyish and romantic heart. He is deeply scholarly and learned, often becoming so absorbed in theological studies or biographies that he loses track of time and domestic details. Though generally soft-spoken and detached, he possesses a strong inner conviction and a fierce protective streak for his children, despising emotional insincerity and calculated social expectations.

_Sources: [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c9 P86](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0086), [v5 c9 P88](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0088), [v5 c14 P18](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0018), [v5 c21 P2](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0002), [v5 c26 P22](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0022)_

- Fulfill his late wife's wish to love and protect their small daughter Ida  <sub>[v5 c14 P19](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0019)</sub>

## History

John Ashdown serves as the Presbyterian minister at Glen St. Agnes. Following the unexpected death of his beloved wife Cecilia, he was left to raise their children—including Tobias, Grace, Ida, Rupert, and Gerald—while managing his pastoral duties. During a walk through Fern Hollow to take a drink from a hidden spring, he engaged in a heart-to-heart conversation with young Edmund Carrow, forming a close friendship with the boy. Shortly after, he encountered Clementine Ainslie by the spring in the moonlight, seeing her clearly for the first time and finding comfort in her presence during subsequent visits. When the wealthy Mrs. Hector Twiss abruptly demanded to adopt his daughter Ida, John grew fiercely defensive and refused to part with his late wife's child. Later, when his son Rupert fell critically ill with double pneumonia after a night spent in the cemetery, John kept a night-long vigil and called for Dr. Carrow's aid until the boy safely recovered. Over the winter, realizing his deep affection for Clementine, he set out through Fern Hollow intending to express his feelings to her.
